main.title: Super Mario Odyssey
main.subtitle: Cappy opens new ways to explore
main.summary: Super Mario Odyssey pairs Mario with Cappy for a journey through open kingdoms full of Power Moons and creatures to capture.

cards.heading: Mario and Cappy travel together
cards.text: Super Mario Odyssey is Nintendo?s 2017 3D platformer for Switch, released on October 27. Mario travels between kingdoms with Cappy, a living hat that can attack, support jumps and capture creatures or objects. Power Moons found throughout the kingdoms help move the journey forward.

cards.heading: Adding the hat to a jump
cards.text: Throwing Cappy hits enemies, activates switches and breaks objects. Mario can also bounce from the hat to extend a jump. Different throw directions combine with dives and somersaults, letting experienced players reach platforms by less obvious routes.

cards.heading: Capturing different abilities
cards.text: Capturing a creature gives Mario its abilities. A Bullet Bill flies across gaps, a Cheep Cheep swims underwater and a Sherm supplies another way to interact with obstacles. Each capture introduces controls suited to its part of a kingdom.

cards.heading: Searching for Power Moons
cards.text: Many Power Moons are available in the same area at once. Players find them through movement challenges, conversations, hidden paths and experiments with Cappy. Exploring a kingdom can uncover several objectives without returning to a separate mission selection screen.

cards.heading: Contrasting kingdoms
cards.text: The kingdoms range from prehistoric ruins and deserts to snowy landscapes and New Donk City. The city?s realistically proportioned inhabitants contrast with Mario, while its streets and skyscrapers offer climbing and jumping routes. Familiar movement links these different surroundings.

cards.heading: Costumes and photographs
cards.text: Crazy Cap shops sell costumes using coins and local currencies. Photo mode lets players pause, adjust the framing and record the places they have reached. Different outfits and kingdoms offer many combinations for these pictures.

cards.heading: Mario and Cappy share the controls
cards.text: In cooperative play, one player controls Mario and the other controls Cappy. The hat can attack, collect objects and assist Mario?s movement independently. Director Kenta Motokura described Cappy?s relative safety as useful for players with less experience.
